desc:
The array nums has n + 1 elements and every element lies in the range 1..n. Exactly one value occurs more than once (it may occur two times or many more times); every other value occurs at most once. Return the repeated value.

Do not modify nums, and use only O(1) extra space.

Example: nums = [1, 3, 4, 2, 2] returns 2.
constraints: Exactly one value occurs at least twice; all other values occur at most once
hints: A set or a count map finds the repeat, and sorting does too, but both break one of the rules (extra memory or modifying the array). Look for a different way to view the array.

Treat index i as a node with one outgoing edge to nums[i]. Every value is at least 1, so index 0 is never the target of an edge. Two different indices pointing to the same node means a node with two incoming edges.

Start at index 0 and keep jumping i = nums[i]. The walk must end up in a cycle, and the entrance of that cycle is the repeated value. Find the meeting point with a slow and a fast pointer, then restart one pointer from 0 and move both one step at a time until they meet.
editorial: Build the functional graph i -> nums[i]. It has n + 1 nodes (0..n) and every edge goes to a node in 1..n, so the walk from node 0 can never return to 0 and must eventually loop. Node 0 has no incoming edge; the cycle entrance is the first node on the cycle, and it is reached once from the tail and once from the cycle, i.e. it has two incoming edges, meaning two indices hold the same value. Two incoming edges to one node is exactly a repeated value, and since only one value repeats, the cycle entrance is the answer.

Floyd's cycle detection finds the entrance in O(1) space. Phase one: move slow one step and fast two steps from index 0 until they meet inside the cycle. Phase two: put slow back on 0 and advance both one step at a time; if the tail has length a and the meeting point is a steps before the entrance when measured around the cycle, they meet exactly at the entrance.

Alternatives: a hash set is O(n) space, sorting modifies the array, and binary search on the value range (count how many elements are ≤ mid) is O(n log n) time and O(1) space without modifying the input.
